intro: Most Romanians are Orthodox Christians who speak a Latin-based language, and millions of them now live and work in other European countries.

chapters.title: People and languages
text: Bucharest is the capital and largest city, followed by Cluj-Napoca, Timișoara and Iași. Romanian is the official language; there is a large Hungarian minority in Transylvania, and a Roma community.
Millions of Romanians have moved abroad to work, especially in Italy, Spain, Germany and the UK.

chapters.title: Faith and traditions
text: Most Romanians are Orthodox. In northern Moldavia, monasteries are covered inside and out with colourful painted scenes. On 1 March, people give each other mărțișor, a red and white token, to welcome spring.

keyTerms.meaning: A red-and-white token given on 1 March to celebrate spring.
